issues.description: The commented example usage in the template Main.java shows constructors with two parameters for Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the problem UML and the reference solution expect constructors that only initialize the animal's name (single-argument). This discrepancy can confuse students about the required constructor signatures and which attributes each animal class should have.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent: update the template Main.java commented examples to use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML and solution implementation, or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to explicitly require and document the additional constructor parameters if those extra attributes are intended.

issues.description: Constructor usage in the template Main.java shows Animal subclass constructors being called with two arguments (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem statement/UML and the solution implementation use single-argument constructors that take only the animal's name. This mismatch between the example usage in the template and the intended constructor signatures can confuse students about the required constructor parameters and which attributes the classes should initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the example constructor calls in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java consistent with the UML and solution by using single-argument constructors (name only), e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky"). Alternatively, if a second attribute is intended, update the UML/problem statement and solution to include that attribute and a matching constructor.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares a private helper method singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (signature currently omits the parameter), while the UML/problem statement and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This discrepancy in the method signature between the template and the specification/solution can obstruct students from correctly implementing the verse printing logic and mapping the UML to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so it matches the UML/specification and the solution; update the method body to use the passed-in animal when printing the verse.
